parsed.answer: No past ticket reports this exact problem. The crash is PowerShell 7's own update notification code (UpdatesNotification.ShowUpdateNotification) throwing 'totalWidth (-17) must be a non-negative value' from String.PadRight. This most likely happens because the console window is very narrow when pwsh starts, so the computed padding goes negative. The existing tickets are different issues: #16301 is a PowerShell crash caused by an embedded NUL in environment variables, fixed in Terminal 1.19.10302.0, and the others are Terminal's own crashes. As a workaround, you can disable the update check by setting the environment variable POWERSHELL_UPDATECHECK=Off, or start pwsh with -NoLogo. You can also make the window wider at launch, for example by increasing the initial columns in Terminal settings. Please report this to the PowerShell repository (PowerShell/PowerShell), since the fault is in pwsh rather than Windows Terminal.
